description.narrative: Oour Voices Our Futures (OVOF) will use capacity-building and convenings among feminist movements to strengthen and build movements within countries and across regions, while also link feminist movements to relevant actors, such as internet rights’ movements, Dutch allies and progressive policymakers. OVOF believes in strengthening movements from within, to create more inclusive, powerful and resilient movements. To influence laws and policies at national and international levels, OVOF sees this as the only sustainable mitigation strategy in relation to the increasing power of anti-rights and anti-gender forces.

(1 Joint activity reported on behalf of OVOF) OVOF participation at ILGA World Conference. The ILGA World Conference is a global gathering of activists, advocates, and allies committed to advancing the rights of LGBTQIA+ individuals. This year, the conference made a historic return to Africa for the first time in 25 years, hosted in the vibrant city of Cape Town, South Africa. This year's conference was an important milestone, bringing together a diverse array of voices from across the world to engage in critical discussions, build solidarity, and strategize for the future of LGBTQIA+ rights. Among the attendees was the OVOF, represented by consortium members, the secretariat and partners who attended multiple sessions and engaged with the global community. This conference was a significant platform that allowed for conversations and amplifying voices of structurally silenced women. It provided a platform to learn from diverse advocacy strategies, especially around intersectionality and inclusive solidarity, which can be integrated into OVOF’s approach. Additionally, the conference highlighted the importance of participating in international forums to ensure OVOF’s work is not only recognized but also supported through partnerships and collaborations that advance the rights of marginalized groups across regions. This conference was a great networking opportunity that led to establishing new connections with global activists, allies, and organizations doing similar work. It also gave access to innovative strategies and tools that can inform OVOF’s future work. By attending sessions and interacting, there has been a strengthened capacity to advocate and amplify the voices of SSWs even more. The demonstrations by South African activists during the ILGA World Conference serve as a critical reminder of the need for meaningful local representation in international spaces, especially when hosted in their country. (1 CREA activity) In May 2024, 200 Sex workers from 5 South Asia countries (India, Nepal, Pakistan, Srilanka and Bangladesh) gathered for the first time and got a platform to discuss the issues. The summit recognised the extraordinary contribution of sex worker movements in realising civic rights and entitlements for sex workers and breaking systemic and structural barriers. The summit was a celebration of the power of collectivisation, the strength and resilience of diverse sex worker movements in the region, and the joy and inspiration we get from the arts. The outcome was the Kathmandu Declaration This Declaration calls upon governments, multilateral agencies, the United Nations, civil society organisations, and law and policy makers to commit to advancing sex worker rights and respect the voices of democratic and inclusive movements led by sex workers over the last 30 years across these countries, recognise that sex workers’ rights are human rights, recognise sex work is work among other demands. The Declaration was taken to AWID where 900 AWID participants signed up in solidarity with the South Asia sex workers. Crea’s allyship with the South Asia sex workers movement was documented in the form of a case study in the new Crea publication called Feminist Allyship. OVOF supported the printing of this publication in English and e-versions in 8 languages including South Asia languages. OVOF also supported documentation of the Renew event by OVOF partner in the form of blogs.

As a consortium, OVOF will conduct 3 regional partner convenings in 2023 and 2024 to connect the various local partners with each other to network, learn and collaborate, and will organise 2 activists convenings including exploring possibilities to expand the Changing Faces Changing Spaces Pan-African Conference to other OVOF regions.
